definition.en: The nose, the windpipe and the lungs: the parts of the body that take in oxygen from the air and give out carbon dioxide.
definition.zh: 鼻、气管和肺：身体里从空气中吸进氧气、放出二氧化碳的那些部分。

definition.en: The heart, the blood and the blood vessels: they carry digested food, oxygen and carbon dioxide to and from every part of the body.
definition.zh: 心脏、血液和血管：把消化后的食物、氧气和二氧化碳运到身体各处，再运回来。

definition.en: Breathing in and breathing out. When the chest gets bigger, air flows into the lungs; when it gets smaller, air flows out.
definition.zh: 吸气和呼气。胸腔变大时，空气流进肺里；胸腔变小时，空气流出去。

definition.en: The tube that carries air from the throat down to the lungs. Rings of cartilage keep it open. Also called the trachea.
definition.zh: 把空气从咽送到肺的管子，一圈圈软骨让它保持张开。英文也叫 trachea。

definition.en: The two large organs in the chest, one on each side of the heart. In the lungs, oxygen from the air goes into the blood and carbon dioxide comes out.
definition.zh: 胸腔里的两个大器官，心脏两边各一个。在肺里，空气中的氧气进入血液，二氧化碳从血液出来。

definition.en: A pump made of muscle, in the middle of the chest. Each beat pushes blood into the blood vessels.
definition.zh: 在胸腔正中、由肌肉构成的泵。每跳一下，就把血挤进血管。

definition.en: The liquid that flows round the body in the blood vessels, carrying digested food, oxygen and carbon dioxide. It is always red: bright red with much oxygen, dark red with little.
definition.zh: 在血管里流遍全身的液体，运送消化后的食物、氧气和二氧化碳。它总是红色的：含氧多时鲜红，含氧少时暗红。

definition.en: A tube that carries blood. Some carry blood away from the heart and some bring it back. The names artery, vein and capillary are beyond the syllabus.
definition.zh: 运送血液的管子。有的把血从心脏运出去，有的把血运回心脏。动脉、静脉、毛细血管这些名称超出课纲。

definition.en: A gas that makes up about 21 per cent of air. The body takes some of it into the blood in the lungs.
definition.zh: 约占空气 21% 的一种气体。身体在肺里把其中一部分吸收进血液。

definition.en: A gas that makes up about 0.04 per cent of air and about 4 per cent of breathed-out air. Body parts give it out, and the blood carries it to the lungs.
definition.zh: 约占空气 0.04%、呼出气体 4% 的一种气体。身体各部分放出它，血液把它带到肺。

definition.en: The gas that makes up most of the air, about 78 per cent. The body breathes it in and out without using it.
definition.zh: 空气里最多的气体，约占 78%。身体把它吸进、呼出，但不使用它。

definition.en: Water in the form of a gas. How much air holds depends on the weather; breathed-out air has more.
definition.zh: 气态的水。空气里有多少，要看天气；呼出的气体里更多。

definition.en: The things a living thing does to stay alive, such as growing, moving and responding. Body parts use digested food and oxygen to carry them out.
definition.zh: 生物为了活着所做的事，例如生长、运动、作出反应。身体各部分用消化后的食物和氧气进行这些过程。

definition.en: The thin, folded parts on each side of a fish's head that take in oxygen dissolved in water and give out carbon dioxide.
definition.zh: 鱼头两侧很薄、多褶的部分，吸收溶在水里的氧气，放出二氧化碳。

definition.en: The tubes that branch from the bottom of the windpipe into the lungs, getting smaller and smaller. The syllabus does not ask for the name.
definition.zh: 从气管下端分出、通进肺里、越分越细的管子。课纲不要求这个名称。

definition.en: The dome-shaped muscle under the lungs. It moves down when you breathe in, making the chest bigger. The syllabus does not ask for the name.
definition.zh: 肺下面圆顶形的肌肉。吸气时它往下移，让胸腔变大。课纲不要求这个名称。
